  "text": "The call came once more, then ceased. In the quiet after it, she heard water dripping from the kettle onto the hearth.

Elias turned his hands over.

“Have you kept the garden?”

“Most of it.”

“The beans?”

“They wouldn't climb this year.”

He nodded, as though he might go out after tea and see what could be done.

Mara fetched the sugar bowl. The spoon lay buried in it, its handle showing. She dug it free and put two spoonfuls into his mug.

“One,” he said.

“You used to take two.”

“Did I?”

She sat opposite him. Beyond his shoulder, the little cupboard hung crookedly. For seven years she had meant to ask someone to straighten it.

“Your coat,” she said. “You'll be warm.”

He looked down at the buttons but made no move to undo them.

On the table between his wrists was a pale crescent, left by a hot saucepan long ago. Mara covered it with the sugar bowl.

“I was angry,” she said.

“The table was new.”

“Not about the table.”

He watched her. Outside, someone dragged the basket across the bricks. A child called a question, and another child answered.

“You should drink,” she said.

Elias bent toward the mug. For a moment she thought he was smelling the tea.

“It's good to be here.”

She reached across and took his sleeve between finger and thumb. The cloth was dry, rough at the seam. She had expected something else, though afterward she could never remember what.

“There's bread,” she said.

He glanced toward the window.

“I'll cut it thin.”"
